text:
maya: Need to provision a new GPU nodepool in us-west1 for the embedding/recall workload. Target latency-sensitive small-batch inference, predictable p99. Considering A10G primary with an H100 burst pool for large jobs. Who can help with quotas and cluster-autoscaler behavior?

alex: How many concurrent pods and GPUs per pod are we expecting? rough numbers will help sizing.

maya: Expect ~60 steady pods doing 1 GPU each for embeddings (short sequences). Occasional Batch jobs might want 4+ GPUs (big models) but rare. So target ~70 GPUs baseline, with 20-30 burst capacity.

jon: For that mix I usually do: primary pool = A10G, nodes with 1 GPU each (better bin-packing), burst pool = H100 preemptible with 4 GPUs per node. Autoscaler policies: prefer `least-waste` expander and set max node count tightly.

priya: FYI cluster-autoscaler config we used in prod (snippet):
```yaml
--cloud-provider=gce
--scale-down-delay-after-add=10m
--expander=least-waste
--max-node-provision-time=20m
```
Set `scale-down-delay-after-add` longer for GPUs so pods don't bounce.

carlos: Also make sure to use taints+tolerations for the H100 pool (e.g., `gpu-burst=true:NoSchedule`) and label nodes `gpu-type=h100|a10g` so schedulers/PodAffinity pick preferred pool.

maya: Good. What about quota? I checked console and our current regional GPU quota in us-west1 is low.

infra-bot: quota-checker: region us-west1 current GPU quota = 80, used = 42, available = 38. Max per-sku quotas: A10G=40, H100=16. (automated check)

alex: So we need quota increases if we want ~90 total with some headroom. Open a GCP quota request for A10G + H100 in us-west1, request numbers: A10G -> 60, H100 -> 32. Include justification: low-latency embeddings + occasional batch.

jon: Cost tradeoffs: A10G is ~0.8x H100 for perf/cost on embeddings. If we can use 1 GPU per pod A10G looks cheaper. H100 should be reserved only for the rare heavy-retrain/batch jobs.

priya: Nodepool naming convention proposal: `np-gpu-a10g-usw1-prod-v1` and `np-gpu-h100-usw1-burst`. Include kubelet flag or resource accounting: set `--feature-gates=DevicePlugins=true` and enable the GPU device plugin DaemonSet.

maya: Good. Any concerns about cluster autoscaler picking the burst pool too often? We want CA to prefer A10G unless pod requests label `gpu-type=h100` or tolerates the burst taint.

priya: Two levers: 1) Use `expander=least-waste` and node group min/max tuned, 2) use `priorityClass` on H100 pods or explicit nodeSelector. Also set `max-total-unready-percentage=40` so CA doesn't overprovision into creating too many nodes when startup is slow.

carlos: For preemptible H100 nodes, set a longer `scale-down-unneeded-time` and `scale-down-unready-time` to avoid churn from preemption.

alex: Quick sanity check command to probe node labels once pool exists: `kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=np-gpu-a10g-usw1-prod-v1 -o wide`

maya: I'll open the quota ticket and draft the nodepool Terraform. Assigning: @alex to collect cost estimates + vCPU/cpu requests per node, @jon to write autoscaler config, @priya to prepare nodepool TF + taints/labels, @carlos to validate preemptible safeguards.

infra-bot: ticket-created: INC-4321 (quota request submitted). Link: https://console.cloud.google.com/quotas?project=redwood-inference

maya: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll sync with bizops for the budget sign-off.

jon: One more note — remember GPU allocatable varies; account for ~0.9 GPU per node for scheduling if device-plugin uses fractional? double-check device-plugin behavior for A10G.

priya: Yep will add a kube-scheduler predicate and set realistic requests/limits in the pod spec to avoid overcommit.

maya: closing loop — we'll aim to have TF + quota approved by EOD Wednesday.

alex: ack, starting cost calc now.

carlos: ping if you want me to submit quota escalation in the partner form to speed it up.

maya: thanks, team.
